title: Multivalent supramolecular fluorescent probes for accurate disease imaging

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The introduction argues that hydrophilization strategies are inadequate because increasing renal clearance 'shortens their circulation half-life, thus restricting their use primarily to renal disease imaging (13)', and the stated advance of this work is a probe that evades MPS capture and achieves 'prolonged bloodstream circulation'. Yet the same probe is claimed to deliver 'substantial advancements in the early diagnosis of acute kidney injury' — i.e., precisely the renal-disease application that the authors attribute to rapidly renally cleared (short-circulating) probes. As written, the design rationale and the claimed AKI application are in tension and no mechanism reconciling long circulation with renal lesion contrast is given in the visible text.
